question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: an MCP initialize (jsonrpc 2.0, protocolVersion 2025-06-18, clientInfo plumb-probe 1.0), then tools/list, Accept application/json and text/event-stream

decoded.serverInfo: firecrawl-fastmcp 3.26.0. The 2026-09-22 record of this surface names 3.25.2 and the 2026-09-09 one 3.24.1: three distinct versions in twenty days
decoded.tools-list-keyless: 200 with exactly firecrawl_scrape, firecrawl_search and firecrawl_parse, the same three names as on 2026-09-22 and 2026-09-18. What a stranger may call has not changed while the server's version has changed twice
decoded.instructions-string: the server's own instructions differ from the 2026-09-18 archive in three places, all inside that string: "indexed repositories" became "indexed public repositories"; "curated documentation sites" became "code documentation"; and a clause is appended that names a tool and a concept no earlier reading here carries, "and firecrawl_find_tools as the progressive Alexandria catalogue lookup alongside the Alexandria options of firecrawl_search and firecrawl_scrape for catalogued data providers". The rest is character for character the same
decoded.comparison-basis: the comparison is against the 2026-09-18 transcript, which is the most recent one archived. The 2026-09-22 pass recorded the version string and the tool names but archived no bytes, so the two phrase changes and the appended clause cannot be dated more precisely than between 09-18 and 09-29
decoded.rest-403: POST https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/scrape with no Authorization answers 403 with the same sentence as 2026-09-22 including the parenthesis addressed to machines, and carries www-authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://www.firecrawl.dev/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource". No earlier record here lists this response's headers, so whether the challenge on THIS endpoint is new is unknown
decoded.not-measured: no tool was called, so this pass does not re-test the KEYLESS_ACCESS_NOT_AVAILABLE refusal of 2026-09-22; firecrawl_find_tools and the Alexandria catalogue are named only in the instructions string, are described there as needing a key, and were not exercised

finding: With no credentials on 2026-09-29, the Firecrawl MCP server answers initialize 200 as firecrawl-fastmcp 3.26.0, where the 2026-09-22 record names 3.25.2 and the 2026-09-09 one 3.24.1, and a keyless tools/list still returns exactly firecrawl_scrape, firecrawl_search and firecrawl_parse. What a stranger may call has not moved through three server versions in twenty days; what the server says about itself has. Against the 2026-09-18 transcript, the instructions string changes two phrases and appends a clause naming firecrawl_find_tools and an "Alexandria catalogue" that no earlier reading here carries, both described as keyed. The 2026-09-22 pass archived no bytes, so those changes can only be dated to between 09-18 and 09-29. No tool was called and nothing was registered.

reproducibility.command: curl -s -X POST https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"plumb-probe","version":"1.0"}}}'; curl -s -X POST https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -H 'mcp-protocol-version: 2025-06-18' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}'
